genericProblem: Candidate selection controls were designed per screen, risking inconsistent query semantics, pagination, cascading cleanup and error recovery across otherwise similar business choices.
rootCauseClass: The P6 search audit classified controls by individual page but did not elevate the repeated cross-owner candidate-query interaction into a consumer-protocol invariant.
finiteDenominator: IA01 invitation role candidate query/page branch
counterexamples: Fixed state/type enumerations and a latest detail's immutable facts are not candidate searches.
A shared consumer query shape must not merge owner authorization or permit browser-derived candidates.

findings.statement: Growing, duplicate-prone or relationship-constrained choices require one consumer candidate-query protocol rather than page-local query designs.

Invitation business-role candidates lack the unified protocol's owner queryText, page, pageSize and context-token semantics, so a full readback or client filter cannot be treated as searchable selection.
